intro: Water, energy and nature: how natural phenomena are told, and how to say that one thing depends on another.
p.sequía.consejo: It is written with q: «se-KI-a». The accent on the i separates the two vowels.
p.inundación.consejo: The verb is «inundar». You say «inundarse» when water gets into a place.
p.incendio.consejo: A «incendio forestal» burns a forest. A small fire, like the kitchen one, is «fuego».
p.tormenta.consejo: A storm brings thunder and lightning; a «temporal» lasts days with wind and rain.
p.cosecha.consejo: The ch sounds «ch»: «ko-SE-cha». The verb is «cosechar»; it is not «coser».
p.embalse.consejo: In Spain you also say «pantano». It fills with rain and river water.
p.renovable.consejo: Same for masculine and feminine: «energía renovable». Its opposite is «no renovable».
p.residuos.consejo: It is almost always plural: «residuos plásticos». They are sorted to be recycled.
p.recursos naturales.consejo: Water, sun and forests are natural resources. Some of them can run out.
p.agotarse.consejo: With «se»: «el agua se agota». A person can also run out of energy: «estoy agotado».
p.ecosistema.consejo: It is written as one word: «ecosistema». «Eco-» comes from Greek and means «home».
p.extinguirse.glosa: to die out, to go out
p.extinguirse.consejo: It is said of a species or a fire. It takes «se»: «el fuego se extinguió».
p.talar.consejo: It is regular. Felling many trees at once causes deforestation.
p.preservar.consejo: It means almost the same as «proteger». You preserve the environment.
b1.texto:
**The phenomena.** A **sequía** is a long period without rain; an **inundación**, too much water where it should not be. There are also **incendios**, **tormentas** and bad **cosechas**. The **embalse** stores river water.

**Things that happen by themselves.** With **se**: el río **se desbordó**, el fuego **se extinguió**, el agua **se agota**, una especie **se extingue**.

**Nature.** **Recursos naturales** can **agotarse**. We must **preservar** the **ecosistema**, not **talar** without thinking and sort the **residuos**. **Renovable** energies (solar, wind) do not run out.

**Arguing.** **Cuanto más… más…**: the more the temperature rises, the drier the ground gets. **De + infinitive** (= if): **De seguir así…** **Mientras / es urgente que** + subjunctive.
b2.f0.texto: The reservoir is at ten per cent of its capacity.
b2.f1.texto: We have gone three years without a good harvest.
b2.f2.texto: The more the temperature rises, the drier the ground gets.
b2.f3.texto: It is urgent that we save water at home.
b2.f4.texto: I will water only at night for as long as the drought lasts.
b2.f5.texto: Renewable energies also help to preserve natural resources.
b2.f6.texto: If things go on like this, the resources will run out soon.
b2.f7.texto: If we take care of the ecosystem, the harvest will return.
b4.titulo: Cuanto más… más…, de + infinitive and mientras
b4.texto:
**Cuanto más… (más…)** says one thing grows or falls according to another: **Cuanto más llueve, más sube el río.** Also with **menos**: **Cuanto menos llueve, menos agua hay.**

**De + infinitive** replaces **si** and is used to warn: **De seguir así, el río se secará** (= if we go on like this).

**Mientras + subjunctive** marks a limit in the future: **Regaremos de noche mientras dure la emergencia.** For something happening now, **mientras + indicative**: **Mientras llueve, leo.**
b4.e0.texto: The more it rains, the higher the river rises.
b4.e1.texto: If it rains little, the reservoir will not fill.
b4.e2.texto: We will water at night for as long as the emergency lasts.
b5.f0.texto: The water of the reservoir drops every summer like a slow tide.
b5.f1.texto: Its cracked banks look like the skin of a very old animal.
b5.f2.texto: Among the mud the broken roofs of the village the waters covered peek out.
b5.f3.texto: A hot wind lifts red dust over the empty fields.
b5.f4.texto: The farmers look at the sky with tired eyes and wait for a cloud.
b5.f5.texto: One October afternoon the storm finally arrives, black and heavy.
b5.f6.texto: The first drops hit the hard ground like small stones.
b5.f7.texto: The smell of wet earth rises from the field and fills the air.
b5.f8.texto: The dry earth cannot drink so much water all at once.
b5.f9.texto: The brown water leaves the streams and runs between the houses.
b6.o0: Cuanto más llueve, tanto sube el río
b6.o0.refuerzo: The pattern is «cuanto más…, más…», not «tanto».
b6.o1: Cuanto más llueve, más sube el río
b6.o2: Cuanto más llueve, que sube el río
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Que» does not work here: you need «más».
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is indicative: it describes a present fact, not a limit.
b7.o2.refuerzo: After «mientras» the future is not used.
b7.pregunta: Which form does «mientras» take for a future limit?
b8.frase: De seguir así, el río se secará
b8.traduccion: If things go on like this, the river will dry up
b9.o0.refuerzo: That would be a flood, not running out.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Cleaning has nothing to do with running out.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «agotarse» is running out until nothing is left.
b9.pregunta: What does it mean that the water runs out?
b11.frase: Es urgente que nadie ____ más árboles.
b11.o0.refuerzo: That is indicative; «es urgente que» takes the subjunctive.
b11.o2.refuerzo: That is future; after «es urgente que» comes the subjunctive.
b11.pregunta: Which form does «es urgente que» take?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the sun does not run out, so it is renewable.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Coal runs out when burnt: it is not renewable.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Oil runs out: it is not renewable.
p.capacidad.consejo: The most a container can hold, from «capaz».
p.ahorremos.consejo: Subjunctive of «ahorrar» after «que», for a needed action.
p.regaré.consejo: Future of «regar» for «yo»: the «é» marks the future.
p.dure.consejo: Subjunctive of «durar» after «mientras», for a time that continues.
p.energías.consejo: Plural of «energía», the power that makes things work.
p.renovables.consejo: Plural of «renovable», which can be replaced naturally.
p.ayudan.consejo: Third person plural of «ayudar», to help.
p.seguir.consejo: «Seguir así» means to continue like this.
p.recursos.consejo: Plural of «recurso», something useful we can use.
p.agotarán.consejo: Future of «agotarse», to run out; «-án» marks the future.
p.cuidamos.consejo: From «cuidar», to take care of: the «c» before «u» sounds like «k».
p.emergencia.consejo: An urgent situation that needs quick action; the «g» before «e» sounds like «h».
p.marea.consejo: The rise and fall of the sea: «marea alta» is high tide.
p.orillas.consejo: Plural of «orilla», the edge of water.
p.agrietadas.consejo: Feminine plural of «agrietado»: full of cracks, from «grieta».
p.piel.consejo: The outside layer of a body; «ie» is one syllable here.
p.barro.consejo: Earth mixed with water: the mud left after a flood.
p.asoman.consejo: From «asomar», to show above or from behind something.
p.cubrieron.consejo: Third person plural in the past of «cubrir», to cover.
p.aguas.consejo: Plural of «agua»: the singular takes «el», but the plural takes «las».
p.octubre.consejo: Months in Spanish are written in lowercase.
p.arroyos.consejo: Plural of «arroyo», a small stream of water.
p.casas.consejo: Plural of «casa», a house or a home.
p.regamos.consejo: Present of «regar» for «nosotros»; «regar» means to water plants.
p.secará.consejo: Future of «secar», to dry up; the «á» marks the future.
p.tale.consejo: This is not a real Spanish word; it is a typo.
